To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people react positively to highly-personalized, targeted ads, and would be willing to share personal data to obtain them".

(1) people are willing to share their data with advertisers if it results in highly-personalized advertising; (2) people are more willing to share data with advertisers if they are made aware that the data will be used to generate highly-personalized advertisements; (3) people are more likely to share data with an advertiser if the data will be shared with only one advertiser, compared to if they are made to believe that the data will also be shared with other advertisers.

1) people would share their personal data with online ad providers in exchange for highly personalized ads; 2) people would be willing to share more personal data in exchange of ads that are perceived as more personalized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question "what is the value of highly-personalized advertising?"
the question: would people be willing to trade their personal data in order to get personalized online ads?
the question of how to design personalized ads that are more acceptable to users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
highly-personalised ads are a promising approach for increasing the acceptance of data sharing for advertising purposes.
the more personal and relevant the advertisement, the more likely people are to accept sharing their personal information with advertisers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants would not mind being tracked and their data would be shared with advertisers in order to receive highly-personalized advertisements.
people are willing to share more data if they get more value from it."
people are willing to share their data in exchange for ads that are highly-personalized and that are perceived as being relevant to them.

, when people are exposed to highly-personalized advertising, they may feel that the ad is "talking" to them, and that it is "knowing" them.
people are willing to share their private data with advertisers, as long as they receive in return highly-personalized, relevant ads.
